messages:
alex: Heads-up — we got a customer escalation (acct: acme) for p95/p99 regressions on /v1/generate starting ~10:10 UTC. Grafana shows p99 up from 220ms -> 1.8s.

tara: I pulled prefix cache metrics. Miss rate jumped 2% -> 37% at the same time. KV eviction rate also spiked.

kevin: Any deploys around then?

alex: No infra deploys. There was a small SDK release earlier but only client-side.

matt: Support reported a traffic pattern change: large number of distinct X-Client-Session headers from a new mobile client roll. Could be high-cardinality header causing cache key explosion.

tara: I reproduced locally with traffic replay. Repro steps: 1) replay ~1200 rps with unique session header values, 2) observe kv_p95 token latency climb, 3) watch prefix_key_count increase. Command I used: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --timeout 5s http://local:8080/v1/generate -H 'X-Client-Session: rand-<i>'`

kevin: Logs show a cache key normalization bug — header case variants weren't normalized so we ended up with multiple keys per session id (session vs Session vs session-id). Patch in PR #482 fixes normalization and canonicalization.

alex: Nice catch. For short-term mitigation can we: 1) enable header key whitelist to drop high-cardinality headers for affected route, 2) increase prefix cache size by 25% for the autoscaling pool, 3) rate-limit requests per session id at edge?

matt: Support-ops, can you ask customer to rollback the mobile rollout for a few minutes while we stabilize?

support-ops: Reached out to customer. They can throttle rollout to 10% immediately.

tara: Additional notes from repro: when warmup is cold, KV misses cause synchronous disk reads for some shards which cascade latencies. I added a temp circuit-breaker config to return 429 for new session-rich requests when miss rate > 20%: `prefix_cache.circuit_breaker.threshold = 0.20`

kevin: We should also add an anti-thrash backoff: when eviction_rate > X then throttle new unique prefix inserts for T seconds. I'll prepare a small change to the eviction controller.

alex: Action items: 
- kevin: land header normalization hotfix + unit tests (PR 482), backport to current prod tag.
- tara: push circuit-breaker config in staging, test with replay and then promote.
- matt/support-ops: coordinate with acme to pause rollout to 10% now.
- alex: monitor p95/p99 and KV miss rate; if no improvement in 15m, apply cache size bump.

sre-bot: incident assigned to #oncall-eng-runtime (kev-oncall). ETA 15m for hotfix review.

kevin: Hotfix ready for review, small change in header_normalizer.go. Will tag patch release for dedicated pools.

tara: After applying circuit-breaker in staging replayed 2k rps with unique sessions and miss rate stayed under 12% and p99 under 420ms.

alex: Great. Once kevin ships normalization and we confirm customer throttled, we should see steady state. Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause = header key normalization bug + rollout creating high-cardinality keys; contributing = prefix cache eviction policy not throttling unique inserts quickly enough. Remediations = normalization, header whitelist, circuit-breaker, eviction backoff.

matt: I captured a heap of flamegraphs and the sampling trace, uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-debug/acme/4067890123/trace.tar.gz

support-ops: Customer confirms they throttled rollout to 10% and we're seeing p99 drop to ~300ms. They want a short RCA before reopening the rollout.

alex: I'll draft RCA and runbook changes (add whitelist + circuit-breaker+eviction backoff) and share in this thread.

kevin: Merged normalization hotfix, rolling to prod in next 8m.

tara: Monitoring: prefix_miss_rate back to 3%, eviction_rate normalized. Keeping circuit-breaker on for 30m.

alex: Thanks all. Follow-up: include a test in load-tests that simulates header-case variants and high-cardinality headers to prevent regression.
